items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: the bass player was a sub that day actually, he was Sandy Block.

ctx.x: 1952. So we added a drummer to the duo, who was Charlie Smith, and the bass player was a sub that day actually, he was Sandy Block. And sure enough, Bird and Dizzy came on the show and they did “Hot House” and that turned out to be the only sound film that exists of Charlie Parker. And it’s also a very young Dizzy at that point if you look, if you see him. I worked a little bit with Dizzy later on in one thing or another and I remember that Bird came and sat in with us at Tony Scott’s combo at Cafe Society and I…
Most of them are, one way or another.
